newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grain stocks as of Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: Canada grain stocks as of Dec 31.

text.p: Statistics Canada survey of farm and commercial grain stocks on Dec 31 in millions of tonnes, with farm stocks of a year earlier:
'96 FARM STOCKS '95 FARM STOCKS COMMERCIAL TOTAL
'96 FARM STOCKS '95 FARM STOCKS COMMERCIAL TOTAL
Statistics Canada said higher output of wheat and barley was the main reason for the 29.5 percent increase in all-wheat farm stocks and the 20.3 percent in barley farm stocks.
As of the survey date, 63 percent of total production of wheat was stored on farms, compared with 59 percent a year earlier. The ratio for barley was 61 percent, almost the same as a year earlier.

It said since 1993, December wheat farm stocks had fallen from a high of 23.2 million tonnes to a low of 14.8 million last year. This year's 4.4 million tonne jump was the largest in December farm stocks since 1990's 7.7 million tonne rise.

Current on-farm wheat stocks are now just 1.8 percent under the five-year average of 19.4 million tonnes, it said. The rise paralleled a 5.5 million tonne (21.9 percent) increase in the 1996 harvest from 1995.

For barley, Statscan attributed the stock increase to a record output of 15.9 million tonnes. The stock level was 14 percent above the five-year average of 8.5 million tonnes but 15 percent below the record of 11.5 million tonnes in 1982.
Demand for barley from August through December increased, with exports up 107 percent and domestic feed use up 10 percent, it added.
In Western Canada, farm stocks were as follows:
- all wheat 18.990 million tonnes (14.550 million a year earlier)
